claims.statement: Struts' multipart file-upload interceptor binds exactly three properties for an uploaded image — `File img`, `String imgFileName`, `String imgContentType` — declared on `Action4Upload`, which every action class inherits through `Action4Upload → Action4Pagination → Action4Pojo → Action4Service → Action4Parameter → Action4Result`; every uploading form therefore uses `enctype="multipart/form-data"` with a file input named `img`.

The bound `imgFileName` and `imgContentType` values are never read anywhere in the application — only `Action4Upload` itself mentions them — so the pipeline ignores the upload's original name and MIME type and always writes a JPEG.

Only two action classes write image bytes under the web root: `CategoryAction.add`/`CategoryAction.update` and `ProductImageAction.add`; those are the only `ServletContext.getRealPath(...)` call sites in `src/`, and directories such as `img/site` and `img/lunbo` are static assets with no writer.

`Action4Service.saveWithJpg(File)` reads the inherited `img` field, copies the multipart temp file over the destination with `FileUtils.copyFile`, converts it with `ImageUtil.change2jpg`, and writes the result back to that same path with `ImageIO.write(img, "jpg", file)`; its only handled failure is `IOException`, which it logs and swallows, so callers cannot tell whether the file was written.

`ImageUtil.change2jpg` decodes through AWT (`Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().createImage(path)` plus `PixelGrabber` with forceRGB) and rebuilds the image over a `DirectColorModel(32, 0xFF0000, 0xFF00, 0xFF)` that has no alpha mask, so transparency in the upload is discarded, and it returns `null` when pixel grabbing is interrupted.

`ImageUtil.resizeImage(Image,int,int)` builds a new `BufferedImage` of exactly the requested width and height with `TYPE_INT_RGB` and draws `srcImage.getScaledInstance(width, height, Image.SCALE_SMOOTH)` into it, so the derivatives are non-aspect-preserving stretches; the `File` overload reads with `ImageIO.read` and writes format `jpg`, catching only `IOException` while the in-memory overload catches `Exception` and can return `null`.

Both image writers persist the entity first and then derive the file name from the Hibernate-assigned identity id: `CategoryAction.add` writes `img/category/<category.id>.jpg` and `ProductImageAction.add` writes `img/<dir>/<productImage.id>.jpg`, keeping `file.getName()` in a local `fileName` so the derivatives reuse the same name; the row is therefore committed before any byte is written.

`CategoryAction.update` guards the image write with `if (img != null)` while `CategoryAction.add` and `ProductImageAction.add` call `saveWithJpg` unconditionally, so a multipart submit with no file selected is a silent no-op on update and an unchecked failure from `FileUtils.copyFile` on add — after the database row already exists.

`ProductImageAction.add` picks the primary directory with a single if/else on `ProductImageService.type_single`: `img/productSingle` when the type equals that constant and `img/productDetail` for every other value, so an unvalidated `productImage.type` posted from the hidden form field lands in `img/productDetail` and its file is listed by no screen, because the admin list and all storefront readers filter on `type_single`/`type_detail`.

Only `type_single` product images get derivatives: `ProductImageAction.add` calls `mkdirs()` on the two derivative directories and writes `img/productSingle_small/<id>.jpg` at 56×56 and `img/productSingle_middle/<id>.jpg` at 217×190, while a `type_detail` upload gets no resize step at all.

Deleting a product image removes only the database row: `ProductImageAction.delete` calls `t2p(productImage)` and deletes through the service, leaving the primary file and any derivatives on disk as unreferenced orphans.

`ProductImageServiceImpl.setFirstProductImage(Product)` returns immediately when `product.getFirstProductImage()` is already non-null and otherwise assigns element 0 of `list("product", product, "type", type_single)`; because `BaseServiceImpl.list(Object...)` appends `Order.desc("id")`, that element is the highest `productImage.id` — the most recently added single image — and `type_detail` rows are never considered.

`Product.firstProductImage`, `Product.productSingleImages` and `Product.productDetailImages` are `@Transient` fields with no database column; they are filled per request on the read path by `ProductServiceImpl.fill(Category)`, `ForeAction.product`, `ForeAction.search`, `ProductAction.list` and `OrderItemServiceImpl.fill(Order)`.

The read side composes relative URLs from ids it already has, never from the filesystem: admin screens use the iterated `productImage.id` for `img/productSingle/<id>.jpg`, `img/productSingle_small/<id>.jpg` and `img/productDetail/<id>.jpg`, storefront list and cart pages use `img/productSingle_middle/<firstProductImage.id>.jpg`, and the product detail page shows `img/productSingle/<firstProductImage.id>.jpg` as the large image with `productSingle_small` thumbnails whose `bigImageURL` attribute a jQuery `mouseenter` handler copies onto the large image's `src`; `productSingle_small` has no other reader.

When a product has no `type_single` image, `setFirstProductImage` leaves `firstProductImage` null and `${...firstProductImage.id}` renders as an empty string, so a reader emits a URL such as `img/productSingle/.jpg` for a file that was never written — a broken image with no server error and no log entry.

Written files are immediately reachable as URLs because the launcher sets the webapp resource base to the `web/` directory and `ServletContext.getRealPath(...)` in the actions resolves the write path inside that same tree, so `img/<dir>/<id>.jpg` is served as a static file by the container (the `struts2` filter is mapped to `/*` but matches no action for that path).

Static image serving depends on the root rewrite staying exact-match: `StartJetty` installs an anonymous Jetty `Rule` that maps only `"/".equals(target)` to `/forehome`, and the source comment records that a `RewritePatternRule` with pattern `/` has regex/prefix semantics and would rewrite every `/img/...` path to `/forehome`, answering image requests with the home page HTML.

Image rows are ephemeral while image bytes are durable: the in-memory H2 database is re-seeded from `classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql` at every start, the seed inserts explicit `productimage` rows starting at id 629 and calibrates `ALTER TABLE productimage ALTER COLUMN id RESTART WITH 10211` (and `category` with `RESTART WITH 84`), while the seeded ids have committed files under `web/img/**` that `.gitignore` does not exclude — so a runtime upload leaves an untracked file whose row disappears on restart and whose id is handed to the next upload, silently overwriting the leftover.

No automated test covers the image pipeline: the only test class `com.caozhihu.tmall.test.TestTmall` loads `classpath:applicationContext.xml` and drives `DAOImpl` over `Category` only, and never calls `saveWithJpg`, `change2jpg`, `resizeImage` or any action.
